details.publicNotes:
If not for the glowing flames in their eyes and faint embers in their footprints, a lifespark bandit would be almost indistinguishable from a raccoon. Though their habit of taking anything they can get their paws on resembles their animal lookalikes, their internal biology is far more closely related to that of phoenixes.

Lifespark bandits particularly prize objects that are either nonflammable or especially flammable. Items in the former category can survive proximity to the bandit's beloved flames without being consumed, while those in the latter category make excellent kindling for bonfires.

Lifespark bandits are quick to seek revenge for perceived slights. While they prefer to avoid inflicting bodily harm in their revenge, they are capable combatants if cornered. Occasionally, a lifespark bandit takes a liking to those who treat them well. Those who earn the affection of a lifespark bandit might find all manner of goods left as offerings, ranging from trash to items of personal significance to whoever once owned them to stolen fragments of vital essence.

Little Fires Everywhere

When lifespark bandits exact revenge on creatures who have earned their enmity, they often turn to the tool that comes easily to their paws: fire. A lifespark bandit makes note of the items that an enemy seems to value most and then, one by one, destroys those treasured objects in individual acts of arson. Eyewitness accounts of a raccoon fleeing the scene are often ignored.

Suggested Monster Parts

Monster Parts 12/27/50 gp

Eligible Refinements weapons (piercing), armor (light), perception item, skill items (Acrobatics, Athletics, Nature, Stealth, Thievery)

Eligible Imbued Properties bane, burning barbs, charisma, death, dexterity, energy resistant (fire, vitality), fire, fire shield, life, lifeward armor, sensory (darkvision), strength, wild

description.value:
Proximity to fire invigorates the vital essence within a lifespark bandit. Whenever a lifespark bandit's fire immunity negates fire damage, the lifespark bandit becomes invigorated for one minute, granting them 2d6 temporary Hit Points and a +1 status bonus on Fortitude saving throws. When the invigoration ends, any remaining temporary Hit Points are lost. A lifespark bandit can't become invigorated from their own flames or those of another lifespark bandit.

@UUID[Compendium.battlezoo-bestiary-es-pf2e.sf2e-effects.Item.ty6KJvSh2c7ze8yj]{Effect: Invigoration}

Trigger An adjacent creature hits the lifespark bandit with a melee attack

Effect An arc of fire leaps and scorches the triggering creature, dealing @Damage[1d8[fire]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:18|basic] save).

Requirements The lifespark bandit is invigorated

Effect The lifespark bandit sneaks a burning piece of vital essence onto an adjacent creature. The lifespark bandit must attempt a @Check[thievery|against:perception] check against the target's Perception DC. On a success, the target takes @Damage[1d6[persistent,fire]] damage and the lifespark bandit gains a +2 status bonus on damage rolls against this target for as long as this persistent damage lasts, and the lifespark bandit is no longer invigorated.

Requirements The lifespark bandit is not invigorated and has just hit a creature with their claws Strike

Effect The lifespark bandit digs their claws into the creature, attempting to steal its vital essence. The lifespark bandit attempts a @Check[thievery|against:fortitude] check against their target's Fortitude DC. On a success, the lifespark bandit becomes invigorated for 1 minute and the target takes @Damage[1d6[persistent,void]] damage. On a critical success, the target also becomes @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} for 1 hour.
